# synthetic/ — generated fixtures (GPL-3.0-or-later)

These fixtures are **generated by this repository**, not copied from a third
party. They contain no real credentials: the master password, every entry
password and every TOTP seed is a public test constant.

| File | Entries | Master password | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `synthetic-500.kdbx` | 500 | `demopass` | 500-row database for G3 scroll check, M5-03/M3-04 open/list/search performance, and the WebDAV drills (M4-07) |

`synthetic-500.kdbx` is a real **KDBX 4.0** database written through the same
write backend the application uses (`keepassxcr 0.3.1`, via
`keepassity_core::kdbx::writer::write_model`), so it is byte-for-byte a file the
app can open, edit, save and sync. The backend's default key-derivation
parameters are used (Argon2id, 64 MiB memory, 3 iterations, parallelism 2), which
is representative of a real database for open/unlock timing.

## Contents

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Groups | 7 (root `Synthetic 500` + `Personal`, `Work`, `Banking`, `Social`, `Email`, `TOTP`) |
| Entries | exactly 500, spread round-robin over the six child groups |
| Standard fields | `Title`, `UserName`, `Password`, `URL`, `Notes` are non-empty on every entry |
| Non-ASCII titles | 39 entries (`条目`, `Übergang`, `サンプル`, `пример`) |
| Non-ASCII usernames | 30 entries (`用户`, `пользователь`, `ユーザー`) |
| Percent-encoded URLs | 46 entries use `/…%E8%B4%A6%E6%88%B7/…` (non-ASCII path) |
| Custom field | 50 entries carry `Recovery = recovery-NNNN` |
| TOTP | 20 entries carry an `otp` otpauth URI with the public test secret `JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP` |
| History | 10 entries carry one historical revision |
| Deleted objects | 3 synthetic tombstones |

## Provenance and regeneration

Source definition and checks: [`crates/core/tests/synthetic_fixture.rs`](../../../crates/core/tests/synthetic_fixture.rs).

The writer draws a fresh KDF salt, master seed and IV on every save, so
regenerating the file changes its bytes and therefore its SHA-256. The manifest
and the file must be refreshed together:

```powershell
# from the repository root; rewrites the file and the manifest entry, then
# checks every fixture hash
pwsh -File tools/fixture-gen/regenerate.ps1
```

Equivalent manual steps:

```powershell
$env:KEEPASSITY_SYNTHETIC_OUT = (Resolve-Path tests/fixtures/synthetic).Path
cargo test -p keepassity-core --test synthetic_fixture generate_synthetic_500 -- --ignored --nocapture
pwsh -File tools/fixture-gen/regenerate.ps1 -SkipGenerate
```

Normal `cargo test` runs do **not** regenerate anything: they verify that the
committed file still has the documented shape (500 entries, 7 groups, 20 TOTP
entries, non-ASCII values, 3 tombstones). An accidental edit to the fixture is
caught twice — by that test and by `scripts/verify-fixtures.ps1` (SHA-256/size
against `tests/fixtures/manifest.json`).
